taskTitle: NIST SP 800-63B password rules, current revision

checks.detail: 3 subtasks, read from the schema reply
5 phases had the tools designed for them

breakdown.label: topic single-factor-minimum-length: minimum length of a password used as the only authentication factor (characters)
topic maximum-length: the maximum password length verifiers permit (characters)
topic composition-rules: imposing composition rules, such as requiring a mix of character types
topic periodic-change: requiring subscribers to change their passwords periodically
topic password-hints: letting subscribers store a password hint that unauthenticated claimants can see
topic security-questions: prompting for knowledge-based authentication or security questions when a password is chosen
topic blocklist: checking a new password against a blocklist of commonly used, expected or compromised passwords
topic password-managers: allowing password managers and autofill
topic salt-length: the length of the salt used when storing passwords (bits)
topic hashing-scheme: using an approved password hashing scheme from the latest revision of SP 800-132

finalText:
NIST SP 800-63B-4 (Revision 4) sets out these password requirements in section 3.1.1.2, "Password Verifiers". All three workers read the same page, https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html, and their quotes and keywords agree on all ten topics.

Caveats from the workers' reports:
- The page is dated 26 Aug 2025, and its abstract says "This publication supersedes NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-63B." The page has no explicit "Final" label, and nobody opened the nvlpubs.nist.gov PDF to confirm status. I am treating Rev 4 as current because of the supersession statement.
- Nobody opened the Revision 3 text, so I can't say whether it differs. The workers found no conflicts within the Rev 4 page.
- Maximum length is a SHOULD, and 64 is a floor ("at least 64 characters"), not a cap.
- Hashing scheme is only a SHOULD. A separate sentence, "Passwords SHALL be salted and hashed using a suitable password hashing scheme", is a SHALL, but it doesn't name SP 800-132. One worker reported it, and I haven't included it in the JSON.
- The 15-character minimum applies to single-factor use. One worker noted that passwords used only within multi-factor authentication may be shorter, with a minimum of 8. That detail is reported by one worker, and I haven't included its quote.
- One worker also noted the periodic-change prohibition is paired with a requirement to force a change on evidence of compromise.
